 Somalia and Ghana meet in the fourth round of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers on Monday, 16 November, at 15:00 (UK time). The match takes place at Essipong Sports Stadium in Ghana, where Somalia will be the designated home side despite playing away from their own country.
 The Black Stars secured a 2-0 victory in the reverse fixture on Thursday, claiming their first win of the qualifying campaign. Ghana now sit third in Group C with three points, while Somalia remain bottom without a point after three defeats.

 Somalia vs. Ghana - Head-to-head record
 Ghana have dominated the previous meetings between these two nations, winning all three encounters without conceding a goal. 
 The Black Stars recorded two clean-sheet victories against Somalia in 2003 before securing another 2-0 success in their most recent meeting on 12 November 2026.
 That latest result highlighted the difference in quality between the sides, with Ghana controlling much of the contest and scoring in both halves. Somalia will be hoping to produce a more competitive performance in the return fixture, although their historical record offers little encouragement.

 Somalia - Ocean Stars Searching for Their First Points
 Somalia have endured a difficult start to their Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign, losing all three group matches and struggling to create chances. Let’s examine their recent performances and expected line-up ahead of another challenging encounter.
 Recent form
 Somalia began their Group C campaign with a 2-1 defeat away to Gambia before losing 2-0 against Ivory Coast. Their struggles continued on Thursday, when Ghana secured another 2-0 victory to leave the Ocean Stars bottom of the standings without a point.
 Yusuf Ali Nur’s side have scored just once in their last six matches across all competitions, highlighting their difficulties in attack. They have also conceded exactly twice in each of their three group fixtures, leaving them with a goal difference of -5.
 Somalia progressed beyond the preliminary qualifying round after defeating Mauritius on penalties, but they have struggled against stronger opposition since then. Another defeat would leave their hopes of reaching the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time hanging by a thread.
 There are no new injury concerns or suspensions following Thursday’s match. Goalkeeper Ibrahim Ahmed Hussein could retain his place after saving Jordan Ayew’s penalty in the reverse fixture, while Bilal Njie, Abel Gigli and Sakariya Hassan are among those expected to feature again.

 Ghana - Black Stars Looking to Build on First Qualifying Win
 Ghana finally secured their first victory of the qualifying campaign on Thursday, beating Somalia 2-0 after consecutive defeats in September. With their qualification hopes still alive, let’s take a closer look at their recent form and expected line-up.
 Recent form
 Ghana began their Group C campaign with a 2-0 away defeat to Ivory Coast before surrendering a two-goal lead in a 4-2 home loss to Gambia. Those results contributed to Carlos Queiroz’s departure, leaving interim manager Kim Lars Bjorkegren tasked with reviving their qualifying hopes.
 The Black Stars responded with a 2-0 victory over Somalia on Thursday, ending a five-match winless run across all competitions. Jonas Adjetey opened the scoring shortly before half-time after Jordan Ayew had missed a penalty, while Felix Afena-Gyan added a second goal after the break.
 That result marked Bjorkegren’s first competitive victory in charge and Ghana’s first Africa Cup of Nations qualifying win in approximately three years. However, they remain third in Group C , three points behind Gambia and six behind leaders Ivory Coast, making another victory essential.
 Ghana will be without Antoine Semenyo and Jan Gyamerah through injury, but no suspensions have been reported. Thomas Partey, Mohammed Kudus, Mohammed Salisu and Jordan Ayew all returned to the squad for this international window, with the latter three expected to feature again.

 Predictions for Somalia vs. Ghana - Ghana to win comfortably
 Ghana arrive as strong favourites after securing a 2-0 victory in the reverse fixture. Somalia have struggled to create chances throughout the qualifying campaign, making not both teams to score in the first half an appealing option, particularly given the hosts’ limited attacking threat.
 The Black Stars scored once in each half of Thursday’s victory and should have further opportunities against a defence that has conceded twice in every group match. A goal to be scored in both halves is therefore another market worth considering.
 Despite their inconsistent recent results, Ghana possess considerably more attacking quality than their opponents. Our main prediction is Ghana to win with a -2.5 Asian Handicap , requiring the Black Stars to win by at least three goals.
